assessment: This manuscript will appeal to all with an interest in comparative physiology and the molecular biology of age-associated changes in muscle function. The authors draw parallels between aging skeletal muscle in humans and C. elegans, with evidence in support of age-dependent oxidation of the C. elegans ryanodine receptor ortholog, UNC-68, causing loss of the calstabin ortholog, FKB-2. This in turn results in calcium leak, reduced body wall calcium transients and muscle weakness, changes that are similar to those that occur in aging human skeletal muscle despite the dramatic differences in the lifespan of the two organisms.
